meta.purpose: A dated, line-by-line record of what was checked in this session, what came back, and what changed as a result. It exists so that a reviewer can see the difference between a claim that was verified and a claim that was merely repeated from an earlier session.
meta.method: Each supplied link was requested through a client that follows redirects; the final URL, the page title and the breadcrumb were read. Each policy page was requested and quoted directly. Where a page could not be reached, the failure is recorded rather than worked around.
meta.rule: No row is marked confirmed because an earlier session said so. A row is confirmed here only when this session opened the source and read it.

findings.title: The link that failed three times resolved twice
findings.what: P-04 returned Amazon's /checkpoint/continue page on three consecutive attempts in an earlier session. In this session it resolved on both attempts to /dp/B0DHZTCNR5.
findings.means: The link is not dead. Either the interstitial is intermittent, or it is served to some clients and not others. A register that recorded only one of those outcomes would be misleading in one direction or the other.
findings.action: The P-04 record now carries both outcomes, the product is on the site, and the retry is the reason a monthly link check is on the suggestion list.

findings.title: None of the five arrival URLs carried a tracking parameter
findings.what: After following redirects, all five links ended on a bare /dp/<ASIN> address. No tag parameter appeared in any of them.
findings.means: Program Policies 2(b) requires the Associates ID as a parameter in the URL of each link, and Amazon's own help page lists untagged product links as a reason applications are rejected. Whether the redirect service applies the tag server-side could not be observed from outside, so the short links were neither trusted nor declared invalid.
findings.action: The site stopped offering the short links as click targets. Every buy link is now built as /dp/<ASIN>/?tag=shopnow047c-20 from the ASIN observed on arrival, the submitted code is kept in the record, and a build check fails if an untagged Amazon link appears. Attribution is still unconfirmed until a click shows in the report.

findings.title: Two of the five products are thermometers, not one
findings.what: P-04 resolved to a ThermoMaven instant-read probe. P-05 resolves to a CHEF iQ wireless probe set. Amazon's breadcrumb files both under Kitchen Utensils & Gadgets, then Thermometers & Timers, then Meat.
findings.means: The catalogue is three air fryers and two thermometers. Every page that described the site as four air fryers and a thermometer was wrong, and a site that called P-04 the fourth fryer would have been worse.
findings.action: Front page, register, comparison and guides were corrected, the product card now exists, and a thermometer guide was written around the two products.

findings.title: The disclosure clause is unchanged, and the policies page carries a date
findings.what: Operating Agreement section 5 states the required sentence exactly as quoted. The Program Policies page states 'Updated: April 14, 2026' and section 2(b) contains both the tag requirement and the price/availability rule.
findings.means: The two claims the site leans on hardest are current, and a reviewer can re-read both without an account.
findings.action: Quotes re-verified verbatim and kept on the sources page with the date read.

findings.title: Amazon does publish an ASIN definition a reader can open
findings.what: Sell on Amazon states that an ASIN is a unique 10-character alphanumeric code and that it appears after /dp/ in the URL.
findings.means: The earlier flag saying this definition could not be reached was too pessimistic: Seller Central help is behind a sign-in, but the seller blog is not.
findings.action: FLG-011 is closed with this source, and the nine-character code versus ten-character ASIN argument now rests on an Amazon page rather than on an observation alone.

findings.title: The food-safety source is still unreachable
findings.what: The USDA FSIS air-fryer page did not complete a request from this environment, in this session or the previous one.
findings.means: No safe internal temperature appears anywhere on this site, including in the new thermometer guide. A figure from a secondary source would be worse than no figure.
findings.action: The guide says why the number is absent rather than leaving a gap that looks like an oversight. FLG-012 stays open.

findings.title: Google's paid-link guidance is unchanged
findings.what: The outbound-links documentation, last updated 2025-12-10, still says to mark advertisement or paid-placement links with the sponsored value.
findings.means: rel="sponsored nofollow noopener" on every Amazon link remains the documented marking, and a policy citation is still not a paid link and must not carry it.
findings.action: The build check still fails on an unmarked affiliate link and on a policy citation wrongly marked sponsored.

findings.title: Amazon ties the tag to account approval, and sets a content bar
findings.what: The application review page requires at least three qualifying sales in the first 180 days, asks for robust original content with ten posts as a rule of thumb, says applications are rejected if they do not meet the standard, and lists untagged product links among the reasons an application is rejected.
findings.means: The missing tag was not a polish issue. It is a stated rejection reason, and the content bar is higher than 'published something'.
findings.action: Recorded as SRC-07, used to set the first decision gate, and written into the decision dossier as D-03, D-04 and D-17.

findings.title: Several pages described the catalogue as it was yesterday
findings.what: Counts and sentences on the front page, the about page, the register, the capacity guide, the cleanup guide and the executive summary said four of five links were identified and one product was unresolved.
findings.means: A static site does not notice that its own facts moved. Every one of those sentences was correct when written and wrong when read.
findings.action: Corrected in the data and in the templates, and the correction is listed on the front page's dated change log rather than done quietly.
